newsitem.title: USA: Washington Mutual expects Great Western deal to proceed.
newsitem.headline: Washington Mutual expects Great Western deal to proceed.

text.p: Washington Mutual Inc.'s proposed acquisition of Great Western Financial Corp. should proceed as planned even if hostile suitor H.F. Ahmanson and Co. ups the ante, Washington Mutual Chairman Kerry Killinger said in an interview.
"The market's already voting in our favour and momentum is clearly in support of us," Killinger said Wednesday. "We expect to get the shareholder vote June 13 and close soon thereafter."
Great Western and Washington Mutual both took out newspaper advertisements Thursday touting their planned combination as superior to an Ahmanson acquisition of Great Western.
Both bidders are offering stock swaps, but a recent surge in Washington Mutual's stock has wiped out Ahmanson's premium, leading some analysts to believe Ahmanson may sweeten its bid.
Ahmanson has declined to say if it would raise its offer.
Killinger said that Ahmanson had limited success luring Great Western stockholders after previously raising its bid in March and would likely have the same result if it tried again.
"There has already been an adjustment on the hostile offer on this one and the markets have now spoken and said that even with an increase they are favouring our transaction," he said.
"I think it's highly likely that any additional increase that someone might do would be fully disciplined by the capital markets because of the questionable dilutive nature it would have," he said.

Great Western agreed to merge with Washington Mutual in early March in an effort to thwart Ahmanson's hostile bid. Ahmanson responded by boosting its bid and is now offering to swap up to 1.2 of its shares for each Great Western share.

Under Washington Mutual's deal, it would swap 0.9 of a share for each Great Western share. Both bids were worth about $6.7 billion Thursday, with Ahmanson's at $49.35 a share and Washington Mutual's at $49.73 a share.
Killinger said he was confident the shareholder vote would occur on June 13, despite a court hearing May 30 on a request by Ahmanson to delay the vote.

According to court papers made available to Reuters on Wednesday, Vice Chancellor Jack Jacobs of the Delaware Chancery Court approved a request by Washington Mutual to be an intervenor at the hearing.
"Our attorneys say that they are very confident that the June 13 votes will proceed," said Killinger.

Killinger, who is credited with building up Washington Mutual, largely through acquisitions, including the recent purchase of California-based American Savings Bank, said he may be ready for additional acquisitions in California as soon as six months after the deal is closed with Great Western.
"As soon as we are comfortable that operating plans are going along well with Great Western, we'd look at additional expansion in California," he said.
He declined to name any potential acquisition targets or to comment to questions regarding whether Ahmanson would be an attractive acquisition for Great Western.
